summary: Japanese batch embeddings charged higher than estimate due to tokenizer normalization mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer ran a scheduled bulk embeddings job (~180k texts, Japanese) and reports final invoice shows ~41% more token-equivalent units billed than their local estimates. Impact: unexpected overcharge on monthly invoice, blocking budget approval for next run.

Impact:
- Hanami Health billed ~41% higher than customer-side estimate for the same dataset.
- Job used Dedicated pool in ap-northeast-1 with reserved capacity and KV cache warmup.
- Customer requests provisional credit and explanation prior to month-end invoice finalization.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, ap-northeast-1, org id: org-hanami-98
- Model: open-embed-jp-1.0 pinned
- Batch job run on 2026-03-08 02:10:00 UTC (local JST 11:10)

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Customer ran pre-tokenization and size estimate with Kuromoji-based tokenizer (internal pipeline).
2) Submitted batch via Redwood API using multipart batch upload and asked for embeddings.open endpoint with model open-embed-jp-1.0.
3) Customer expected ~2.1M token-equivalents; invoice shows ~2.95M.

Attachments (provided by customer):
- sample input file (small) + their local token counts.csv
- screenshot of console estimate vs finalized invoice lines

Customer request:
- Explanation of why Redwood metering diverges from Kuromoji counts and request for provisional credit while we investigate.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Raised by customer via support form. Provided sample files and account/job ids. Asked for provisional credit and immediate triage.
2026-03-10 Ethan Brooks: Assigned for first-pass triage. Kicked off metering logs export for job run. Asked Eng for tokenizer behaviour confirmation.

2026-03-11 Eng (Nora Kim): Confirmed we saw higher token-equivalent units recorded for the job. Noted prewarm KV-cache tokens accounted separately in hourly buffer. Investigating tokenizer differences (Kuromoji vs model tokenizer).
2026-03-11 Billing Ops (Marco Ruiz): Requested estimated credit amount to present to finance while investigation proceeds.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Exported metering record for job_id 8f9a3c; raw token-equivalent units: 2,947,200. Billing line items: embedding_unit_count=2,947,200; kv_cache_warmup=312,000 (counted as embed-equivalent per hourly buffer policy).

2026-03-11: Compared customer's sample file tokenization: their pipeline (Kuromoji, morphological tokenizer) reports 1.0x tokens compared to BPE-like tokenizer used by open-embed-jp-1.0 runtime. For many compound words and punctuation, Kuromoji collapses groups while our BPE splits differently, increasing token-equivalents for our meterer.

2026-03-11: Found that customer pre-tokenized estimate explicitly used character-level heuristics (chars / 4) as quick estimate; for Japanese that heuristic systematically underestimates; customer's estimator skipped counting kv-cache warmup (we counted warmup prefetch requests as part of metering for reserved pools).
2026-03-12: Replayed small sample through our runtime tokenizer and confirmed average per-document token ratio ~1.38x vs customer's Kuromoji counts for their sample subset (n=150).
Hypothesis: combination of (A) tokenizer differences (runtime BPE vs Kuromoji) and (B) dedicated KV-cache warmup accounting policy explains majority (~40-45%) of delta.

Notes: Metering pipeline correctly recorded per-request token-equivalents. There is no evidence of duplicate postbacks or retry double-counting for this job. Related_billing_policy: reserved_pool_hourly_buffer counts warmup tokens against first run in new hour window.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Applied provisional credit of 40% of the disputed amount to Hanami Health's account while we complete RCA. Finance reference: CR-2026-82. Customer notified and credited; they acknowledged receipt and requested formal RCA.

2026-03-12: Short-term remediation guidance provided to customer: run our token-estimator tool (Console -> Tools -> Token Estimator) on sample inputs and use that as baseline; alternately, mark inputs as pre-tokenized (if available) so runtime doesn't re-tokenize for estimation, but note pre-tokenized paths may change billing semantics.

2026-03-12: Ops action item created: INT-2210 to add clearer doc about language-specific estimation gotchas and to add a note in Console token estimator about Kuromoji vs BPE differences. Estimated delivery: 2026-04-02.

Follow-ups: Engineering to add per-language sample conversion heuristics to Console estimator (github PR linked). Billing team to publish clarification on how reserved KV-cache warmup tokens show on invoice.
